why: Both analyses land on essentially the same shaving-technology, profit-per-shaver hedgehog, the same stop-doing calls (exit lighters, end diversification, cap the disposable, fund premium systems) and all four key brutal facts. Analysis 2 is slightly better calibrated, with an explicit confidence statement, a CONDITIONAL rather than PASS on unproven Level 5 leadership and a stated test that would break the concept, and it answers the central disposables-versus-premium question more directly, though Analysis 1 uniquely flags the outside-pressure risk.
